resources.string: Screenlate needs its accessibility service to draw the bubble over other apps and to take screenshots for text recognition. Open the settings, find Screenlate under installed services and turn it on.
If the Screenlate switch is greyed out (the app was installed from a file), open App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.

Faster in apps that expose their text.

App text is exact, ready almost at once without waiting for recognition, and needs no network, but only works in apps that expose character positions to accessibility services; elsewhere, and for text in images, the screen is recognized as usual.\n\nReading app text is experimental: some apps report wrong character positions, so the highlight can be off or a neighboring word can be found. If that happens, turn it off.
No screenshots and no recognition. Text in images is not read.

The screen is not recognized at all: only text that apps expose to accessibility services is read. Text in images, manga, games and apps that do not expose their text is not read.\n\nSuits e-ink readers, old or weak devices where recognition does not work or is slow, and slow or metered internet: no battery spent on recognition and no data sent.

Not needed by default: turn it on only if small text is not recognized. It sends extra requests to cloud recognition and uses more mobile data.

Sends parts of the screen to cloud recognition separately, at a higher resolution relative to the whole picture, so small text that a full-screen scan misses gets recognized.

On demand: the part under the aim, once the aim rests where nothing was found.

Always: the whole screen in parts with every scan (more traffic).
Keep both. Turning one off is a last resort for weak or busy devices. Cloud recognition uses mobile data (about 0.1–0.4 MB per scan); on-device recognition does not.

Both: the device and the cloud start together. The device quickly reads the text around the aim, so words appear almost at once; when the cloud answers, its more accurate result replaces them. Without network, or if the cloud fails, the device's result stays.

Cloud only: nothing is recognized without network, and words appear only once the server answers.

Device only: works offline but reads vertical text and manga worse; OCR boost is off.
The device reads the whole screen itself only if cloud recognition has not answered in 3 s. Less load and battery use, but words away from the aim show up later. Leave off if speed matters most.
Type a word or paste text
Entries appear as you type. In other apps, select text and choose “Look up in Screenlate” in the selection menu.
Also available in the system settings: Apps → Screenlate → Language.

A free online service translates the sentence around the word. The translation is machine-made and may be inaccurate, and the sentence is sent to the service’s server.

The services are used without an account: Bing (the Microsoft Translator website), Google Translate and the translator built into Microsoft Edge. They do not publish their limits; when one refuses, the next one takes over. Bing’s first request in an hour takes about a second longer, as it first loads a key from its website.
In the popup, 文A shows the sentence’s translation under the header; a second tap hides it. When the recognized text is hidden, 文A is among the first entry’s buttons.
Fills {sentence-translation} with the translation the popup shows, or asks for one and waits up to 5 seconds. Without a translation the field stays empty.
The first service turned on translates. If it fails or does not answer within 3 seconds, the next one takes over. Drag the handle to change the order.
Asks every service that is turned on at once and shows what each one answered and how long it took.

Allow notifications to follow imports and downloads outside the app.

Screenlate needs the notification permission to show the progress of dictionary imports and downloads. It also makes it possible to keep the system from unloading the bubble, which is a separate switch under “%1$s”.
Keep the system from stopping the bubble
The system restarts the bubble\'s service on its own, unless one of these settings stops it to save power. Both are the system\'s own settings: Screenlate only opens them.
On for Screenlate: the system may stop the bubble in the background.
Off for Screenlate: the system leaves the bubble running.
In the list, find Screenlate and turn optimization off for it (\"Don\'t optimize\", \"Unrestricted\" or similar). Apps missing from the list at first are often under \"All apps\".
Some phones also stop background apps through the manufacturer\'s own settings, apart from battery optimization. There, allow Screenlate to start on its own and to run in the background.
On this phone: App launch → Screenlate → Manage manually, with all three options on.
This phone has none of the known startup screens. App info usually leads to battery and background settings.
For e-book readers and other devices with e-paper (e-ink) screens. Black and white, no animations, frames instead of translucent highlights. Overrides the theme.

Enlarge the floating bubble to %1$d dp (if it is smaller) and the popup text by %2$d px? Both stay adjustable. Turning e-ink mode off brings back the previous sizes, unless you change them in the meantime.

This device looks like an e-ink reader. E-ink mode makes Screenlate black and white, without animations. On slow devices or without internet, the bubble can also read only the text of apps, without recognizing the screen.

Every setting goes back to how it was after installation: the bubble and its hidden apps, lookup, Anki and audio with the field templates, the popup with its font, sizes and CSS, translation, the theme, colors and e-ink mode, background work and update announcements. Hints show again. The dictionaries, installed fonts and the app language stay.
All bubble settings go back to how they were after installation, including the hidden apps, the bubble’s size and its place on the screen. A hidden bubble shows again.
Scan length, entries per lookup and the other lookup settings go back to how they were after installation.
The deck, note type, field templates, tags, duplicate handling and audio sources go back to how they were after installation. Nothing changes in AnkiDroid.

The recognized text at the top, definition copying, auto-hide, the font choice, text size and weight and custom CSS go back to how they were after installation. Downloaded and added fonts stay installed.
The 文A button, translation in notes, the order and switches of the services, the language and the favorite languages go back to how they were after installation.
The theme follows the system again, the colors go back to Screenlate\'s own, and e-ink mode turns off, bringing back the sizes it made larger. The app language stays.
The keep-alive notification turns off. Battery and startup settings belong to Android and stay as they are.

All dictionaries are deleted, including the ones you added, and the bundled ones are installed again as after installation, with the default order and switches. Running imports and downloads are cancelled. Installing takes up to a minute; lookups are incomplete until then.

The app closed twice while resetting the dictionaries, so the reset was stopped. Some dictionaries may be left over or missing. Run the reset again with the button at the top of the Dictionaries page.
Screenlate uses its accessibility service to show the bubble over other apps and to read the text under it.

• A screenshot, when you tap the bubble or pull it out. With App text only, only for a picture in an Anki note.\n• The text apps show on the screen, at the same moments, when Read app text or App text only is on.\n• Which app is open and where the keyboard and the system bars are: to hide the bubble in the apps you chose and to keep it off the bars.

• The screenshot goes to cloud text recognition, unless Engines is set to Device. On-device recognition sends nothing.
• The sentence goes to an online translator when you tap 文A or a note template asks for its translation.
• The word and its reading go to the audio sources you chose, for the pronunciation.
• Notes go to AnkiDroid on this device.

The service does not tap or type anything for you. What it reads is not saved: the screenshot stays in memory while the popup is open, a note gets only the part of the screenshot you select, and the logs never hold text from the screen.
